messages:
olivia-support: FYI escalated from @acme - intermittent embeddings dimension errors in TS SDK during high throughput: 'expected dim 1536, got 0'. Happening ~1-2% of requests when batch size >= 32. Ticket #9876 created by support-bot :warning:
support-bot: Ticket #9876 created and linked to thread.
josh-eng: thanks olivia. can you paste the customer request-id (x-rw-req) and a short repro? any consistent pattern (time, region, model)?
olivia-support: request-id: rw-req_8f3a2c. Model: open-103-1536q (1536 dim). Region: us-west1. Spikes during import job that hits 200rps.
li-devex: quick hypothesis: TS SDK batching + client-side retry could be dropping items when a batch flush times out. ask them to try disabling SDK retries and increase timeout as a quick check.
sara-ml: also could be server-side partial-batch handling bug that returns an empty vector for some slots if KV cache/shard boundary is hit. need request/response payloads to confirm.
gabriel-go: i wrote a small repro hitting the vector endpoint w/ concurrent requests and batching:
```ts
// ts repro (node)
import { RedwoodEmbeddings } from 'redwood-sdk';
const client = new RedwoodEmbeddings({ timeout: 1000, retries: 3 });
async function send(n){
  const docs = Array.from({length:n}).map((_,i)=>`doc ${i}`);
  const out = await client.embed({ input: docs, model: 'open-103-1536q' });
  console.log(out.vectors.map(v=>v.length));
}
// run with concurrency 20 and n=64 repeatedly
```
this reproduces a few zeros after ~2000 loops locally.
nate-ts-sdk: quick note — the TS SDK uses a per-batcher timeout flush and then resolves promises by index. there's a race if a flush triggers while user-level timeout fires and the retry re-enqueues the request into a new batch without preserving the original placeholder. that can cause index misalignment and the client to interpret a missing vector as length 0.
josh-eng: good catch nate. can you dump the SDK debug logs for one of the failing runs? need correlation of batch ids and promise ids.
nate-ts-sdk: attaching sample log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:13.123Z] batcher#42 flush id=42 size=64
[2026-03-10T14:02:14.130Z] request p=abc123 timeout -> retry enqueued
[2026-03-10T14:02:14.131Z] batcher#43 add p=abc123 index=63
[2026-03-10T14:02:14.132Z] batcher#42 response id=42 served=63
[2026-03-10T14:02:14.133Z] resolve p=abc123 with vector=null
```
shows resolve with null.
li-devex: workaround for customer: set retries=0 and timeout=5000ms, or lower batch size to 16. both reduce incidence. we'll need an SDK fix to make retries idempotent w/ per-request tokens.
sara-ml: on server side we should also validate returned vector length != 0 and return 5xx instead of 200+null vectors so client retries are safer. i'll open an internal PR for that behavior change.
josh-eng: action items: 1) nate — implement per-request id token so retry will dedupe in batcher (ENG-1127), 2) sara — server validation and non-200 on empty vectors, 3) support — ask customer to try workaround and collect a failing trace (x-rw-req + full client SDK debug), 4) infra — throttle/concurrency limits guidance in docs.
infra-bot: created issue ENG-1127 in internal tracker assigned to nate-ts-sdk and sara-ml.
olivia-support: I pushed the workaround to customer (retries=0, timeout=5s, batch_size=16). they ran import and reported no more dimension errors after 30m. customer happy for now but asked for ETA on permanent fix.
josh-eng: Nate, estimate?
nate-ts-sdk: will prioritize — aim for a fix in next SDK patch (v0.13.2) in ~5 business days; server change in parallel. short-term patch: ensure that when a timeout triggers we attach the original per-request token and preserve index mapping even across retries.
li-devex: will add a quick note to troubleshooting docs about disabling retries for bulk imports and recommended batch sizes per model dim.
ogabriel-go: i can add a Go/py repro to our internal suite to prevent regressions.
olivia-support: flagged customer as notified. closing escalation when fixes land. :white_check_mark:
